Knowledge-base entry for 'Diaporthe':
────────────────────────────────────────
For stem canker, initial symptoms are small, reddish-brown lesions near the nodes in the lower third of the canopy that expand into sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins; for pod and stem blight, the most characteristic sign is linear rows of black specks on mature soybean stems.. Mature plants with stem canker can exhibit irregular, thin black lines or 'zone' lines on the interior of lower stems; black specks (pycnidia) appear in linear rows on stems for pod and stem blight.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Phomopsis':
────────────────────────────────────────
Phomopsis-infected seeds are cracked and shriveled and often covered with chalky, white mold. Infected seedlings have reddish-brown, pinpoint lesions on the cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.. Seeds are cracked and shriveled with chalky white mold covering; seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on stem near soil line.
────────────────────────────────────────

Knowledge-base entry for 'Bacterial_Blight':
────────────────────────────────────────
Small, angular, reddish-brown lesions surrounded by a yellow halo; as disease progresses, lesions often grow together to produce large, irregularly shaped dead areas.. Centers of older lesions frequently fall out, causing leaves to appear tattered; symptoms usually begin in the upper canopy on young leaves.. Knowledge-base entry for 'Phytophthora':
────────────────────────────────────────
Early symptoms include seed rot and damping off; the most characteristic symptom is a dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, which can girdle the stem causing stunting or death.. A dark brown lesion on the lower stem extending up from the taproot, reaching as high as several nodes, girdling the stem; as disease progresses, damping off, stunting, yellowing, and brown lesions on lower stem can occur.. DISCRIMINATING: 'Diaporthe' vs 'Phomopsis'
Ruling feature : Linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on stems vs. chalky white mold on cracked/shriveled seeds
Diaporthe: Diaporthe produces sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins on lower stems, and most distinctively, linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems; interior of lower stems may show irregular thin black 'zone' lines.
Phomopsis: Phomopsis is characterized by cracked, shriveled seeds covered with chalky white mold, and infected seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.
Decision rule  : IF black specks arranged in linear rows are visible on mature stems, suspect Diaporthe (pod and stem blight); IF seeds are cracked and shriveled with chalky white mold or seedlings show pinpoint reddish-brown lesions on cotyledons, suspect Phomopsis seed/seedling infection.

DISCRIMINATING: 'Green_stem_disorder' vs 'Phomopsis'
Ruling feature : Presence of chalky white mold on cracked/shriveled seeds and reddish-brown lesions on seedlings (Phomopsis) vs. no describable visual markers (Green stem disorder)
Green_stem_disorder: No description is available for Green Stem Disorder, so no visual markers can be identified from the knowledge base.
Phomopsis: Phomopsis shows cracked, shriveled seeds covered with chalky white mold; infected seedlings display reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown streaks on the stem near the soil line.
Decision rule  : IF seeds are cracked and shriveled with chalky white mold, OR seedlings show reddish-brown pinpoint lesions on cotyledons or reddish-brown stem streaks near the soil line, THEN identify as Phomopsis; IF none of these signs are present and no other description matches, the sample cannot be confirmed as either disease from available knowledge.

DISCRIMINATING: 'Green_stem_disorder' vs 'Diaporthe'
Ruling feature : Presence of linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) and/or sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins on stems
Green_stem_disorder: No description is available for Green Stem Disorder, so no specific visual markers can be cited from the knowledge base.
Diaporthe: Diaporthe shows either sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish-brown margins near lower nodes (stem canker) or characteristic linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature stems (pod and stem blight), with possible thin black 'zone lines' inside lower stems.
Decision rule  : IF the stem displays linear rows of black specks and/or sunken gray-brown cankers with reddish margins, THEN classify as Diaporthe; if neither feature is present and no description matches, Green Stem Disorder cannot be visually confirmed from available knowledge-base data.
